nonLabourLines.description: Stripe integration/testing fees and sandbox costs
Data migration tooling / temporary Oracle-to-target ETL licenses

assumptions: No historical actuals (real spend data) are available yet for this project; estimate is based on backlog sizing and rate card only.
Story points roughly map to effort: 1 point ≈ 8-10 hours of blended team effort, adjusted per task type (integration/migration tasks weighted heavier for QA/DevOps).

Backend Developer (1.5 FTE) carries the largest share of work (auth, RBAC, payment integration, migration logic) — at 620 hours over an assumed ~10-12 week delivery window this is roughly 1.2-1.4 FTE utilization, within capacity but leaves little slack for rework.

QA Engineer is only 0.6 FTE; 220 hours allocated is proportionate to that capacity but means QA is a likely bottleneck, especially around PW-7 (payments) and PW-8 (migration) which both need heavy verification.

DevOps Engineer is only 0.4 FTE (effectively ~2 days/week); 90 hours covers CI/staging setup (PW-1) plus light support for migration cutover, but leaves minimal buffer for production incident response during the payment/migration go-live.
PW-8 (Legacy data migration, 21 points) is treated as the highest-risk, highest-effort backlog item, driving a large share of Backend and QA hours and the pessimistic-scenario spread.
Non-labour costs cover Stripe sandbox/testing fees, temporary ETL/migration tooling licenses, and staging/CI cloud infrastructure; these are estimates and could shift with actual vendor quotes.
Scenario spread (10th/50th/90th percentile) reflects uncertainty typical of a project with no actuals yet, wider on the pessimistic side due to migration and payment integration risk.
Frontend Developer (1.0 FTE) hours assume full-time dedication across the design system, dashboard, invoice UI, and RBAC UI work.
input.reasoning: Effort was sized per backlog item using story points as a proxy for relative complexity, then translated into role-hours based on the nature of each task (e.g., PW-8 migration is Backend+QA heavy with light DevOps; PW-2 design system is Frontend-heavy; PW-1 CI/staging is DevOps-heavy). Hours were checked against each role's FTE capacity to flag over/under-staffing risk. Labour lines were computed at the exact rate-card hourly rates. Non-labour costs were added for third-party/tooling costs directly tied to specific backlog items (Stripe, ETL tooling, CI infra). The Most Likely scenario equals the sum of all labour and non-labour lines; Optimistic and Pessimistic scenarios were derived by applying roughly -13%/+19% swings reflecting schedule and scope risk, weighted toward the upside risk given the two Urgent/high-risk items (payments integration and legacy migration) and the thin QA/DevOps staffing.

reductions.description: Descope PW-2 (Design system and component library) to a minimal component set now, deferring full theming tokens and advanced dialog/table variants to a later phase.
reductions.effect: Reduces Frontend Developer hours by ~65 hours; ships a functional but leaner design system, with polish deferred post-launch.

reductions.description: Reduce QA Engineer allocation on lower-risk Medium-priority items (PW-2, PW-6) in favor of concentrated coverage on PW-3/PW-7/PW-8, cutting overall QA hours.
reductions.effect: Cuts ~50 QA hours from lower-risk items; relies more on developer self-testing and automated tests for those features, slightly raising defect risk there.

reductions.description: Defer Legacy Data Migration (PW-8) reconciliation/validation tooling spend and instead reuse existing open-source ETL scripts rather than licensed tooling.
reductions.effect: Removes the dedicated ETL/migration tooling line item; increases manual validation effort slightly but avoids license cost.

reductions.description: Delay non-critical DevOps hardening (e.g., advanced staging environment monitoring) until after initial go-live, keeping only the minimum CI/staging setup required for PW-1.
reductions.effect: Reduces DevOps Engineer hours by ~20 hours; staging environment will have basic monitoring only until a follow-up phase.
